## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, which breaks the case-insensitive key rule that `get` depends on, so any mixed-case key written through the new method can never be read back.

## Changes
The pull request adds a public `Cache.set(key, value)` method, raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds and updates its comment to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — After `c.set("Alpha", 1)`, `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None` because `set` stores `"Alpha"` while `get` looks up `key.lower()`. The class comment at `app/cache.py:14-15` says "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". `get` also deletes only the lower-cased key, so a mixed-case entry is never removed. — Callers that pass mixed-case keys always miss the cache, and their entries stay in `_store` forever, so memory grows without limit. — Fix: Store under `key.lower()`, and in `test_set_then_get_round_trip` set a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"`, because the current test sets `"alpha"`, which is already lower-case, so it cannot catch this defect.
